question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e. **'But'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most **appropriate option** to fill in blank number 1 is 4) but.
 
• The word** "but"** is used to introduce a contrast or contradiction in the sentence.
 
• **In this context,** it is used to indicate that the natural process of learning to walk and talk does not apply to reading.
 
• **The sentence** before the blank states that children learn to walk and talk naturally, implying that it is an innate ability.
 
• However, the use of **"but" **highlights that the same natural process does not apply to reading.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *Children learn to walk and talk naturally, (1) but that is not the case with reading. Reading strategies are designed to help your child develop a strong reading (2) ________ one built with confidence engagement and joy. As a parent, you are most likely always looking for (3) _____ that make your child want to learn. We are here to help you and your child on their journey as a (4) ________ reader. Try some reading strategy suggestions below for kids (5) _______ are beginning to read all the way to those reading advanced chapter books.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Because: **This option does not fit well in the sentence because it does not provide a contrasting idea. It would imply that the reason for children learning to walk and talk naturally is because of reading, which is not the intended meaning.
 
• **Rather:** This option does not fit well in the sentence because it does not provide a contrasting idea. It would imply that children learn to walk and talk naturally instead of reading, which is not the intended meaning.
 
• **When: **This option does not fit well in the sentence because it does not provide a contrasting idea. It would imply a temporal relationship between learning to walk and talk and reading, which is not the intended meaning.
